newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Coconut Oil-Market seen sliding as supplies mount.
newsitem.headline: Coconut Oil-Market seen sliding as supplies mount.

text.p: Coconut oil prices are expected to drop this week as three ships carrying fresh supplies of the commodity from the Philippines had left the country, Manila vegetable oil traders said.
"Some 120,000 tonnes of Philippine coconut oil are scheduled to be shipped to both the U.S. and Rotterdam this month," said one trader.

Three ships, MV Luctor, MV Blue Sapphire and MV Sun Sapphire, left Philippine ports last week and are now on their way to Rotterdam and the United States to deliver an estimated 95,000 tonnes of coconut oil.
Another ship is also expected to arrive shortly in the Philippines to load another 25,000 tonnes, said one trader.
The fresh supplies are expected to boost dwindling supplies of the commodity in Rotterdam.
Rotterdam stocks dropped to 10,223 tonnes as of June 9 from the previous week's 11,948.
Traders said they expected Philippine coconut oil exports to surge as harvests in the second half of the year are seasonally higher.
Philippine coconut oil exports from June 1 to 10 reached 58,000 tonnes compared to 40,543 for the whole month of June 1996, trade group United Coconut Associations of the Philippines Inc said.
